1. Core Clinical Tension: An immunocompetent 8-month-old infant presents with extensive, diffuse hyperkeratotic crusted plaques mimicking severe pediatric eczema, psoriasis, or ichthyosiform dermatoses, accompanied by household contact transmission of pruritic finger-web papules in both parents.
2. Admission Breakpoint: The breakpoint is positioned immediately after physical examination characterizing the diffuse hyperkeratotic palmoplantar and groin eruption and eliciting family contact history, strictly prior to skin scrapings and cutaneous biopsy.
3. Differential Distinctions: Severe atopic dermatitis or seborrheic dermatitis frequently occurs in infancy but typically spares the palms and soles from thick hyperkeratotic crusts and does not contagiously transmit pruritic interdigital papules to adult caregivers. Psoriasis or hereditary keratodermas are ruled out by the household clustering and dramatic microscopic identification of ectoparasites.
case_prompt:
An 8-month-old male infant was evaluated for a 3-month history of a generalized, progressive cutaneous eruption. The infant had been born at 39 weeks gestation following an uncomplicated pregnancy and delivery, had reached normal developmental milestones, and had not received prior medications.

Family and contact history revealed that approximately 2 to 3 months following the onset of the infant's rash, both parents developed an intensely pruritic erythematous papular eruption localized to their interdigital web spaces and the lateral aspects of their fingers without crusting. In addition, the infant's babysitter was noted to have a generalized crusted dermatosis.

Physical examination revealed a well-nourished infant with normal vital signs (temperature 37°C, heart rate 78 beats/min, respiratory rate 28 breaths/min). Dermatologic examination demonstrated diffuse, scaly, crusted, hyperkeratotic, erythematous patches and plaques across the trunk and extremities, with some excoriations. The lesions showed marked predilection and accentuation over the groin, palms, and soles. The remainder of the systemic physical examination was unremarkable.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Infantile atopic dermatitis is a common cause of pruritic, excoriated eczematous plaques, but severe diffuse hyperkeratotic crusting with prominent palmoplantar and groin involvement is atypical. Furthermore, eczema does not transmit as an acute pruritic interdigital rash to adult household contacts.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Diffuse, scaly, crusted, hyperkeratotic, erythematous patches and plaques were seen over the body. Some of the lesions were excoriated. The lesions were accentuated on the groins, palms, and soles... Family history revealed that both parents had an intensely pruritic erythematous papular eruption affecting the interdigital web spaces and lateral aspects of fingers

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Widespread hyperkeratotic plaques in an infant can suggest an inherited keratinization defect or infantile psoriasis; however, the delayed onset at 5 months of age and clustered presentation of pruritic papules in cohabiting parents and caregiver point directly to an infectious/contagious infestation.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: His past medical history was otherwise unremarkable, and he had not been on any medications until 8 months of age which was 3 months after onset of the rash... Family history revealed that both parents had an intensely pruritic erythematous papular eruption affecting the interdigital web spaces and lateral aspects of fingers approximately 2 to 3 months after the onset of the eruption in the infant.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Direct microscopic examination of mineral oil skin scrapings and subsequent histopathological examination of a skin biopsy demonstrated abundant epidermal ectoparasites and ova, establishing the diagnosis of crusted scabies.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Direct microscopic examination of skin scrapings revealed numerous scabies mites and eggs. A skin biopsy was performed on one of the lesions which revealed the scabies mite within the epidermis (Figure 4). A diagnosis of crusted scabies was made.

editor_comments: Standardized admission diagnostic case for crusted scabies in an infant. The admission breakpoint stops immediately prior to bedside skin scraping and biopsy, strictly avoiding pathogen and disease names.
